entries.reason: the release carries no command event class at all: read with tools/mach32_methods.py from the 6.1.3 armv7 cache, none of its 236 classes in the MediaPlayer image at 0x31fe3000 has a name holding CommandEvent and none of its 41 categories adds one, with a nonsense selector absent as the control; and all 236 were read and none declares this member's selector. That is a per-class answer, which is what decides a member: the release's whole-cache selector list (selectors_armv7.txt, 113981 distinct names) has a line for repeatType, shuffleType and isNegative because other frameworks declare those names, which is the trap facts/MediaPlayer/MPMediaItem.md:105 records for albumTrackNumber. A class the release does not have is new code and cannot shadow anything, so there is nothing native for it to be. The command that produces it is already carried, and iOS 6's UIEventTypeRemoteControl has no repeat-mode subtype, so the port's bridge never sends one and the command had no answer at all
entries.effect: NSClassFromString answers the class, and the port's own MPChangeRepeatModeCommand (carried, 8.0) now has the event class its bridge builds lazily by class, so a handler set on that command is handed an event of this class
